pathways.name: Type I Interferon Pathway
pathways.description: Central pathogenic pathway in SLE. TLR7/TLR9 activation by nucleic acid-containing immune complexes triggers plasmacytoid DCs to produce IFN-α, which signals through IFNAR1/IFNAR2 to activate JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/STAT2 → IRF9 → ISG transcription.

pathways.name: B Cell Receptor Signaling & Survival
pathways.description: B cells are central to SLE pathogenesis. Autoreactive B cells escape tolerance checkpoints due to defective receptor editing and enhanced survival signals. BAFF/BLyS overexpression drives B cell survival. BCR signaling through BTK, BLK, and BANK1 promotes activation.

pathways.name: JAK-STAT Signaling
pathways.description: Multiple cytokines implicated in SLE signal through JAK-STAT pathways: type I IFNs (JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/2), IL-6 (JAK1/JAK2 → STAT3), IL-12/IL-23 (JAK2/TYK2 → STAT4), IL-21 (JAK1/JAK3 → STAT3). STAT4 risk variants enhance IL-12/IFN-α signaling.

pathways.name: NF-κB Inflammatory Pathway
pathways.description: NF-κB is a master transcriptional regulator of inflammation. TNFAIP3 (A20) normally limits NF-κB activation through deubiquitination. Loss-of-function TNFAIP3 variants in SLE result in unchecked NF-κB activity, driving proinflammatory cytokine production.

pathways.name: Complement System & Immune Complex Clearance
pathways.description: Defective clearance of apoptotic debris and immune complexes is a hallmark of SLE. Complement C1q deficiency is a strong monogenic cause of SLE. FCGR2A and FCGR3A variants impair IgG-mediated clearance. ITGAM (CD11b/CD18) mutations reduce phagocytosis.

pathways.name: T Cell Costimulation & Follicular Help
pathways.description: T cells provide help to autoreactive B cells through costimulatory interactions (CD40L-CD40, OX40-OX40L, ICOS-ICOSL). TNFSF4 (OX40L) is upregulated in SLE. T follicular helper (Tfh) cells are expanded in SLE and correlate with autoantibody levels.

pathways.name: Endosomal TLR Sensing of Nucleic Acids
pathways.description: TLR7 (ssRNA) and TLR9 (CpG DNA) in endosomes recognize self-nucleic acids in immune complexes. This activates IRF5/IRF7-driven IFN-α production in pDCs and drives B cell activation. TLR7 gene duplication causes human lupus; hydroxychloroquine blocks endosomal TLR activation.

pathways.name: NETosis & Neutrophil Extracellular Traps
pathways.description: NETosis is a programmed neutrophil cell death that releases neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) — webs of chromatin and antimicrobial proteins. In SLE, NETosis is dysregulated: NETs persist due to impaired DNase I degradation and serve as a source of autoantigens (dsDNA, histones, LL-37). NETs activate pDCs via TLR7/TLR9 to produce IFN-α and directly damage endothelial and renal tissue in lupus nephritis.

pathways.name: Complement Cascade (Classical & Terminal)
pathways.description: The full complement system is central to SLE pathogenesis. C1q, C2, and C4 initiate the classical pathway via immune complex recognition and opsonize apoptotic cells. Their deficiencies (especially C1q and C4A) are the strongest monogenic SLE risk factors. Terminal pathway activation produces C3a/C5a (anaphylatoxins) and C5b-9 (MAC), causing tissue inflammation and damage. Paradoxically, early component deficiencies cause SLE while terminal pathway activation drives tissue injury — creating a therapeutic paradox.

pathways.name: Autophagy & Cellular Homeostasis
pathways.description: Autophagy is a conserved cellular degradation pathway that maintains lymphocyte homeostasis, clears damaged mitochondria, and regulates type I IFN production. ATG5 polymorphisms are associated with SLE. Impaired autophagy leads to accumulation of damaged mitochondria and mitochondrial DNA, which activates the cGAS-STING pathway and TLR9, driving IFN production. Autophagy also regulates plasma cell survival and autoantibody secretion.
